q: Which statement best describes the Internet?
options: A single large computer owned by ARPA
A worldwide network of interconnected networks
A software suite that displays web pages
An acronym for International Network of Terminals
explain: The Internet is a worldwide network of interconnected networks. The word is not an acronym.

q: In which year did ARPANET become operational?
explain: ARPANET became operational in 1969. The year 1983 is when it adopted TCP/IP.

q: On 1 January 1983, ARPANET adopted which protocol suite, often called the birth of the modern Internet?
explain: The switch of ARPANET to TCP/IP on 1 January 1983 is the milestone often called the birth of the modern Internet.

q: Who are widely called the Fathers of the Internet for co-designing TCP/IP?
explain: Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn co-designed TCP/IP. Tim Berners-Lee is linked with the Web, not the Internet itself.

q: Radia Perlman, who developed the Spanning Tree Protocol (STP), is popularly called which title?
options: Father of the World Wide Web
explain: Radia Perlman developed STP, which prevents loops in Ethernet networks, and is popularly called the Mother of the Internet.

q: On which date was India's public Internet service formally launched?
explain: Public Internet service in India was formally launched on 15 August 1995; a pre-launch service had begun a day earlier, on 14 August.

q: In which year did Tim Berners-Lee propose the World Wide Web while working at CERN?
explain: He proposed the Web in 1989. The working system followed in 1990 and the public announcement in 1991.

q: What is the full form of W3C, founded by Tim Berners-Lee in 1994?
explain: W3C stands for World Wide Web Consortium; it develops open web standards.

q: Which is the address of the first website, created by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN?
explain: The first website was hosted at info.cern.ch. CERN is the institution, while info.cern.ch is the website address.

q: The public Internet announcement of the World Wide Web project was made in which year?
explain: The public announcement came on 6 August 1991. 1989 was the proposal, 1990 the working system and 1994 the W3C.

q: Which technology defines the structure and content of a web page?
explain: HTML (Hyper Text Markup Language) gives a page its structure and content. CSS handles appearance and JavaScript handles behaviour.

q: Which statement about HTML is correct?
options: It is a programming language that controls page behaviour
It is a style sheet language for appearance
It is a protocol for sending web requests
It is a markup language, not a programming language
explain: HTML is a markup language that describes structure; it is not a programming language. Web requests use HTTP.

q: Which statement about authentication is correct?
options: It determines which actions a user may perform
It stores small records on the client side
It verifies identity, for example with a password, OTP or biometrics
It reduces the time taken for a download
explain: Authentication verifies who you are; authorization decides what you are allowed to do.

q: In the Browser Object Model (BOM), which object handles the URL?
explain: window.location handles the URL, history handles navigation, navigator exposes browser information and screen describes the display.

q: Which was the first web browser, created by Tim Berners-Lee in 1990 and later renamed Nexus?
explain: WorldWideWeb ran on a NeXT computer and was renamed Nexus to avoid confusion with the Web itself.

q: Which well-known browser, begun in 1992, is text-based?
explain: Lynx is a well-known text-based browser that began in 1992. Mosaic was graphical.

q: Which 1993 browser from the University of Illinois, developed by Marc Andreessen, Eric Bina and team, made graphical browsing widely popular?
explain: NCSA Mosaic popularised graphical browsing, although earlier graphical browsers existed, so it was not the first.

q: In which year did Firefox 1.0 arrive?
explain: Phoenix, which appeared in 2002, later became Firefox, and Firefox 1.0 arrived in 2004.

q: Which company acquired Netscape in 1999 (although it did not originally create Navigator)?
explain: AOL acquired Netscape in 1999. Netscape Navigator was created by Netscape Communications in 1994.

q: Which pair correctly defines downloading and uploading?
options: Downloading: remote system to your device; uploading: your device to a remote system
Downloading: your device to a remote system; uploading: remote system to your device
Both mean copying files within the same device
Downloading sends an email; uploading receives it
explain: Download means receiving data on your device; upload means sending data from your device to a remote system.

q: Which statement about Chrome and Chromium is correct?
options: Chrome and Chromium are the same product
Chromium is an open-source browser project started by Google in 2008
Chromium was started by Microsoft in 2008
Chrome is open source while Chromium is not
explain: Chromium is Google's open-source browser project from 2008, and Chrome is a distinct browser.

q: The Epic browser was developed by which Indian-origin company?
explain: Epic comes from Hidden Reflex (original browser 2010, Chromium-based privacy version 2013). UC Browser is from UCWeb.

q: Which technique does Tor use for privacy?
explain: Tor uses onion routing, passing traffic through relays to help hide the source IP address.

q: Which statement about open-source software is correct?
options: All free browsers are open source
Free software is not necessarily open source
explain: Open source means the code is available for inspection, modification and distribution under its licence. Being free of charge does not make software open source.

q: Which shortcut opens a new Incognito window in Chrome on Windows or Linux?
explain: Ctrl + Shift + N opens a new Incognito window. Ctrl + T opens a new tab and Ctrl + W closes the current one.

q: Which statement correctly separates a plugin from an extension?
options: A plugin adds a specialized capability or runtime; an extension adds browser features such as translation
A plugin adds features like password management; an extension adds a runtime for other programs
The two terms mean exactly the same thing
Extensions work only in Tor Browser
explain: Plugins and extensions are related but not identical: plugins add a specialized capability or runtime, while extensions add browser features.

q: Archie, created by Alan Emtage at McGill, indexed which kind of content?
explain: Archie (commonly dated 1990) indexed FTP file listings rather than full web pages.

q: Yahoo began in 1994 as a web directory created by whom?
explain: Yahoo began as a web directory by Jerry Yang and David Filo. Page and Brin founded Google.

q: Baidu, founded in 2000, is a search company from which country?
explain: Baidu is a Chinese search company. Yandex is the Russian one.

q: Who founded YouTube, whose website was registered on 14 February 2005?
options: Larry Page, Sergey Brin and Jerry Yang
Jawed Karim, Jerry Yang and David Filo
Steve Chen, Chad Hurley and Jawed Karim
Gabriel Weinberg, Steve Chen and Chad Hurley
explain: YouTube was founded by Steve Chen, Chad Hurley and Jawed Karim, and it later became part of Google.

q: Which part of a search engine discovers pages and retrieves their content?
explain: The crawler (spider) finds pages and fetches content. The index stores it, ranking selects results and the interface shows them.

q: What does SEM stand for?
explain: SEM is Search Engine Marketing, commonly paid search advertising. SEO is Search Engine Optimization.

q: Which term describes controlled access to selected organisational resources for authorised outsiders such as partners and suppliers?
explain: An extranet gives authorised outsiders controlled access; an intranet is purely internal.

q: Which of the following belongs to the Deep Web?
explain: Private banking dashboards, email and medical records are outside ordinary search indexes, which is the Deep Web. The others are Surface Web.

q: Cookies are small records stored by the browser on which side?
explain: The browser stores cookies on the client side. A server sets them using Set-Cookie and the browser sends them back in later requests.

q: In the URL https://www.example.com/notes, what is '.com'?
explain: https is the scheme, www the subdomain, example.com the domain, .com the top-level domain (TLD) and /notes the path.

q: Which protocol gives clients IP addresses and network settings automatically?
explain: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) assigns addresses and settings. DNS only looks up names.

q: What does the Domain Name System (DNS) do?
options: Delivers web pages in an encrypted form
Looks up records such as IP addresses for domain names
explain: DNS looks up records, such as the IP address that goes with a domain name. Assigning addresses is the job of DHCP.

q: Which statement about packet switching on the Internet is correct?
options: Packets can take different routes and may have different lengths
All IP packets are fixed at 64 bytes
Packet switching reserves a dedicated circuit for each call
Every packet must follow the same single route
explain: Packets can take different routes and vary in length. Reserving a circuit describes circuit switching.

q: Which technology carries voice as digital packets over IP networks and is also called IP telephony?
explain: VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) carries voice as digital packets; WhatsApp voice calls are an example. IRC is for text chat.
